newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Chemical to maintain ethylene output cuts.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Chemical to maintain ethylene output cuts.

text.p: Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said on Tuesday it will maintain its ethylene production cuts in the second quarter of calendar 1997 despite a recent decline in naphtha prices.
"The production cuts are still in effect and we plan to continue them at least through June," a company spokesman said.

Mitsubishi Chemical reduced ethylene output by 10 percent in January in an effort to cool bullish sentiment in Asia's naphtha market and to help boost wholesale prices of its ethylene-derived petrochemical products.

Asia's growing demand for feedstock naphtha pushed up near-term naphtha prices in Asia's benchmark open-specification forward contract by about one-third, or $60 per tonne, in the second half of 1996.
Naphtha prices have been sliding since mid-March, however, and hit a six-month low on Monday, due mainly to weaker crude oil prices and arbitrage cargoes from the West.
Open-spec naphtha for the prompt trading period, currently first-half June, was quoted at $208.00/209.50 per tonne, compared with a peak of $250.00/251.50 on January 10.
Mitsubishi Chemical is Japan's largest petrochemical firm with ethylene production capacity of 1.45 million tonnes per year.
